hero.headline: Vero Beach nonprofit seeks box truck to deliver earthquake relief supplies to Venezuela
hero.teaser: Latinas Nexus Network has collected more than 100 boxes of supplies for Venezuela earthquake relief and needs a box truck by Thursday to transport them to Miami.
hero.body:
A Vero Beach nonprofit organization has collected more than 100 boxes of supplies intended for Venezuela earthquake relief efforts and is now requesting community assistance to transport them. Latinas Nexus Network is partnering with Global Empowerment Mission in Miami to deliver the supplies to Venezuela, which is recovering from a 7.5-magnitude earthquake. The collected boxes contain essential items ranging from diapers to medical supplies.

Lourana Navarro, founder of Latinas Nexus Network, said the community's response to their relief efforts has surpassed what they anticipated. The organization began collecting donations on Friday afternoon and has been overwhelmed by the outpouring of support. Co-founder Juliana Marino expressed the impact of the community's generosity, saying "The community has come together. They all came forward and brought something." However, the volume of donations has created a logistical challenge that the organization cannot solve alone. As Marino explained, the initial plan to transport supplies in their personal vehicles is no longer feasible. "We thought we were just going to put everything in our cars and we were going to drive to Miami. And there's no more room," she said.

To move forward with their mission, Latinas Nexus Network is urgently asking the community to donate the use of a box truck measuring between 12 and 16 feet. They need the truck by Thursday so they can load it and deliver the supplies to Global Empowerment Mission in Miami on Friday. The effort holds deep personal significance for Navarro, who was born in Venezuela and has family members living near the earthquake's epicenter. "It really kills me to see thousands, hundreds of thousands of people in the streets," she said, explaining her commitment to the relief effort.

Despite their determination to help, Navarro and Marino recognize they cannot complete this mission without community support. "We put it together, now we need to deliver," Marino said. Anyone who can help by donating a box truck or providing other assistance should contact Navarro at (954) 205-0700 or Marino at (772) 913-0805. The organization remains focused on ensuring these relief supplies reach the people in Venezuela who need them most.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds surpasses $90 million in fundraising for Florida governor's race
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds has surpassed $90 million in total fundraising, including $23 million raised in the last three months, further cementing his dominance in the GOP field.
cards.body:
Republican gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds has raised more than $90 million for his campaign, solidifying his position as the frontrunner in the GOP primary race. The Naples congressman announced the fundraising totals this week, which include $10 million in his official campaign account and $80 million raised through the Friends of Byron Donalds political committee. The money comes from approximately 37,000 donors. In the most recent three-month period alone, Donalds brought in $23 million. Ryan Smith, the campaign's chief strategist, emphasized Donalds' competitive advantages in the race. "While other candidates run on fumes, Byron Donalds is running full steam ahead," Smith said. "Byron is the clear conservative choice to lead Republicans into the General Election and crush the Democrats and their radical, unaffordable agenda."

The announcement of Donalds' fundraising success coincided with new endorsements from major Florida political figures. Incoming Florida Senate President Jim Boyd and Florida House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison both endorsed Donalds on the same day the fundraising numbers were released. Attorney General James Uthmeier, a former chief of staff to Governor Ron DeSantis, also announced his support for the candidate. Additionally, Donalds has secured an endorsement from President Donald Trump, who encouraged the congressman to enter the race. With Governor Ron DeSantis unable to seek reelection due to term limits, the governorship is open for the first time in eight years.

Donalds faces ten other GOP primary opponents seeking the Republican nomination, including Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, investment manager James Fishback, and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner. Despite criticism from rivals for declining to participate in planned primary debates, Donalds continues to maintain a substantial lead in polling. His campaign has begun an aggressive spending strategy, announcing a $20 million statewide advertising purchase across television and digital platforms. The campaign plans to launch two new television ads that will reach voters throughout Florida.

Beyond advertising, the Donalds campaign has emphasized grassroots organizing efforts. The campaign has already knocked on more than 180,000 doors across the state as it works to mobilize voters. The GOP primary election is scheduled for August 18 and will determine which Republican nominee advances to the general election in November.

cards.headline: Two Killed After Tesla Hit From Behind on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County
cards.teaser: Two people died following a rear-end collision involving a Tesla on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County.
cards.body:
Two people were killed after a Tesla was struck from behind on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County. The fatal crash occurred on the turnpike running through the county.

The Tesla was hit from behind by another vehicle on the turnpike. Both occupants of the Tesla died as a result of the collision.

Authorities responded to the crash scene on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County. The collision resulted in two fatalities.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast celebrates America's 250th birthday with fireworks and festivities Saturday
cards.teaser: America turns 250 years old on Saturday, and communities across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast are pulling out all the stops to mark the milestone.
cards.body:
America turns 250 years old on Saturday, and communities across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast are pulling out all the stops to mark the milestone. From sunrise 5Ks and golf cart parades to drone shows, time capsule openings and spectacular fireworks displays, there is something for everyone this Independence Day.

Delray Beach hosts its annual Fourth of July Celebration on East Atlantic Avenue and A1A starting at 5 p.m., with daytime activities beginning at 8 a.m. The event draws more than 20,000 people and features a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule Opening on the Main Stage at 5 p.m., a 60-foot flag raising with the National Anthem at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue at 6 p.m., and fireworks at 9 p.m. All-day activities include food trucks, vendors, arts and crafts, face painting, carnival games and a photo booth. The event also features a 4's on the 4th Volleyball Tournament from 8 a.m. to noon on the south end of the municipal beach, a sand sculpting contest sponsored by Delray Beach Rotary and Kiwanis Clubs, and snorkeling and scuba dive tours of the S.S. Inchulva Delray Wreck from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. Boca Raton's 68-year-old Independence Day tradition returns with a full day of events. The Firecracker 5K starts at 7:15 a.m. at Florida Atlantic University. The Fabulous Fourth Block Party runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Sugar Sand Park, featuring kids' crafts, yard games, a DJ and food trucks. The Fabulous Finale takes place from 6:30 to 9:30 p.m. at Countess de Hoernle Park, with live music and a 20-minute fireworks display at 9:10 p.m. Lake Worth Beach celebrates with its first-ever drone light show at 8:45 p.m. featuring 300 drones, along with a hot dog eating contest, concerts by Sekond Nature and Elton and the Jets, a skydiving performance by the All Veteran Group, and a fireworks display at 9 p.m. with more than 11,700 shots.

hero.headline: Wellington Green's vacant Nordstrom may become 620-unit apartment complex
hero.body:
Bainbridge Companies has submitted a proposal to transform the 18 acres currently occupied by the empty Nordstrom store at the Mall at Wellington Green into a 620-unit apartment complex. The developer plans to demolish the existing building if the project receives approval from the village. According to Village Manager Jim Barnes, the new development would feature a combination of one-, two-, and three-bedroom units arranged in three towers, along with a dedicated parking structure.

Village officials view the project as part of a solution to address housing shortages affecting not only Wellington and the county but the broader state and region. Barnes emphasized that the area faces a significant need for additional residential units. However, the proposal has sparked opposition from some residents. Richard Meyers, a Wellington resident for over a decade, expressed skepticism about the project, saying the area already has sufficient apartment complexes. Gaby Martinez shared another common concern, warning that the increased density could create traffic problems on local roads. She noted that even routine commuter traffic to the area could cause bottlenecks on surrounding streets.

Village leadership has acknowledged ongoing community discussions about the future of the mall and its relevance in the changing retail landscape. Rather than viewing the apartment complex as a threat to existing retail, Barnes suggested that new residential development nearby could actually benefit the anchor stores and other retailers currently operating at the mall. He pointed out that Macy's, Dillard's, and JCPenney continue to perform well despite broader challenges facing traditional shopping malls. Barnes highlighted that the Macy's location at Wellington Green is the highest-performing store in the state, suggesting the mall maintains commercial viability.

At this stage, the project remains in the proposal phase with no approval granted. The village has not announced a timeline for the project's development or provided a cost estimate for the conversion. The plans are still under review and will require village approval before moving forward.

cards.headline: Boca Raton businesses continue Venezuela earthquake relief donations
cards.teaser: GalaFresh Supermarket West Boca Raton and Doctor Chicha restaurant are collecting supplies and monetary donations for families affected by last week's earthquakes in Venezuela.
cards.body:
Franky Jorge, owner of GalaFresh Supermarket West Boca Raton, moved quickly after hearing about the earthquakes in Venezuela and is now accepting supplies and monetary donations. "Apart from many of our customers being from Venezuela, all of our friends from Venezuela, being Latino, we really feel this as something that really hit close to home," Jorge said.

Pamela Rodriguez, owner of Doctor Chicha, said dozens of volunteers sorted through non-perishable foods, baby supplies, and clothes. The donations will be taken to Global Empowerment Mission in Doral and then shipped to families in Venezuela. Rodriguez said the community's response has been overwhelming and the restaurant was completely full with donations. One volunteer was an earthquake survivor herself who spent four days trapped under rubble before being rescued. As recovery continues, Rodriguez emphasized the importance of continued donations. "The most important thing is to keep donating," she said. Jorge echoed the sentiment, saying "Today it's Venezuela; tomorrow it can be another place and we just want to make sure we're there to assist no matter where it is."

cards.headline: Palm Beach County planners recommend approval of controversial Project Tango AI data center
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County planning staff have recommended that county commissioners approve the controversial Project Tango AI data center, despite months of pushback from residents in the western communities.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card Body

Palm Beach County planning staff have recommended approval of the controversial Project Tango AI data center despite months of resident opposition in western communities. The recommendation does not reflect an opinion on the project, according to Palm Beach County Mayor and Commissioner Sara Baxter, who represents the area where the center would be built. Baxter said the staff recommendation simply means the project has met certain legal criteria required by the county. The proposed data center site sits approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddleview Elementary School.

As part of the approval recommendation, county staff are requiring the applicant to limit potable water use, implement deeper safeguards for lithium iron battery placement, conduct updated sound studies from the Loxahatchee National Wildlife Refuge, and cap daily water use at 100,000 gallons per day. Residents oppose these measures as insufficient. Rachel Smith said the changes amount to "a farce," while Ben Brown questioned why a heavy industrial project is permitted in an area zoned for light industrial use. Baxter, who has publicly opposed the project and must recuse herself from voting, plans to ask fellow commissioners for a moratorium on future data centers. A planning and zoning meeting is scheduled for Thursday, July 2.

Barnes suggested new development near the mall could benefit remaining retailers, noting that Macy's, Dillard's and JCPenney are high-performing stores. He added that the Macy's at the Mall at Wellington Green is the highest-performing store in the state. No timeline or cost estimate has been announced, and the plans have not been approved.

cards.headline: Six Indian River County schools to offer free meals for 2026-2027 school year
cards.teaser: Students at six Indian River County schools will receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs, the district announced .
cards.body:
Students at six Indian River County schools will receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs, the district announced Tuesday. The School District of Indian River County will provide the no-cost meals through the National School Lunch Program and School Breakfast Program, helping families save on daily meal expenses. Fellsmere Academy will offer both free breakfast and lunch to all students throughout the school year. Five additional schools will provide free breakfast only: Pelican Island Classical Magnet, Citrus Elementary, Dodgertown Elementary, Vero Beach Elementary, and Indian River Academy.

Other families in the district may still qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on household size and income criteria. Application letters are being sent to all homes with parents or guardians in the school district. Families can apply by completing the online meal application and returning it to their child's school. For questions about the meal programs, families can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director, at (772) 564-5041 or shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org. The School District of Indian River County offices are located at 6055 62nd Ave in Vero Beach.

cards.headline: Jupiter family pays over $1,000 to fix passport errors before international trip
cards.teaser: Dr. Thomas McCain and his family discovered five errors on their passports after using expedited service and had to travel to Miami to get them corrected.
cards.body:
A Jupiter family is speaking out after receiving passports with multiple errors and spending more than $1,000 to correct them before an international trip. Dr. Thomas McCain contacted WPTV after using the expedited passport system through a local U.S. State Department office. McCain's passport contained one error, while his three children each had the same clerical error. Additionally, the middle name of his middle son was incorrect, totaling five errors across the family's passports. McCain said the errors were discovered a month ago and led to hours of phone calls, dead ends and multiple trips to the Palm Beach Gardens post office. The family ultimately had to travel to Miami to get the passports corrected at a cost exceeding $1,000.

After hearing McCain's story, WPTV contacted the State Department and learned the agency has been undergoing large layoffs and reorganization. A State Department spokesperson stated the department is committed to providing quality service to passport customers while safeguarding U.S. national security. The spokesperson noted that if a Department error is identified, the department will correct it at no charge. Passport holders are encouraged to review their passports upon receipt and promptly report any discrepancies. Standard passports typically cost about $60, and obtaining one without expedited service can take as long as two months.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast communities plan fireworks and celebrations for America's 250th birthday
cards.teaser: Communities across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast are preparing for Independence Day celebrations on Saturday to mark America's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
America turns 250 years old on Saturday, and communities across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast are pulling out all the stops to mark the milestone. From sunrise 5Ks and golf cart parades to drone shows, time capsule openings and spectacular fireworks displays, there is something for everyone this Independence Day.

In Delray Beach, the annual Fourth of July Celebration has been a family-friendly tradition for over 50 years, drawing more than 20,000 people. The event at East Atlantic Avenue and A1A begins at 5 p.m. with additional daytime activities starting at 8 a.m. The celebration features a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule Opening on the Main Stage at A1A, a 60-foot flag raising with National Anthem at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue at 6 p.m., and fireworks at 9 p.m. All day activities include food trucks, vendors, arts and crafts, face painting, carnival games, and a sand sculpting contest.

Lake Worth Beach is celebrating with concerts, a hot dog eating contest at 5:30 p.m., and a skydiving performance by the All Veteran Group at 7:45 p.m., including a tandem jump by Vice Mayor Mimi May carrying a special American flag commemorating the nation's 250th anniversary. The city is celebrating with its first-ever drone show featuring 300 drones for 15 minutes at 8:45 p.m., followed by a fireworks display at 9 p.m. with over 11,700 shots. The Lake Worth Beach Bridge will be closed to vehicles and pedestrians from 8 to 10 p.m.

cards.headline: Vacant Nordstrom at Mall at Wellington Green could become 620-unit apartment complex
cards.teaser: Bainbridge Companies submitted plans to demolish the empty Nordstrom store and convert 18 acres into a multifamily apartment complex.
cards.body:
A plan has been submitted to transform the vacant Nordstrom at the Mall at Wellington Green into a large apartment complex, the village confirmed. Bainbridge Companies submitted plans to convert 18 acres of the empty Nordstrom store into a 620-unit multifamily apartment complex. The existing building would be demolished if the project is approved. Village Manager Jim Barnes said the development would include one-, two- and three-bedroom units with three towers and a parking structure. He said the project addresses a broader housing need throughout the county and state, noting there is a shortage of housing units.

Some residents are not enthusiastic about the proposal. Richard Meyers, who has lived in Wellington for more than a decade, said he opposes adding more apartments to the area, noting there are already apartment complexes around the mall. Other residents raised concerns about the impact on traffic. Barnes noted that several anchor stores continue to perform well despite broader concerns about the mall. He said Macy's, Dillard's and JCPenney are high-performing stores, and he heard that the Macy's at the Mall at Wellington Green is the highest-performing store in the state. No timeline or cost estimate for the project has been announced. The plans have not been approved.

cards.headline: Supreme Court blocks Trump effort to end birthright citizenship in 6-3 ruling
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled that constitutional protection remains in place for children born in the United States, regardless of their parents' immigration status.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday blocked President Donald Trump's effort to end birthright citizenship, ruling 6-3 that the constitutional protection remains in place for children born in the United States, regardless of their parents' immigration status. Trump signed an executive order targeting birthright citizenship on his first day back in office, arguing the move would help repair the nation's immigration system. The order sought to deny automatic citizenship to children born in the U.S. to parents who are in the country illegally. Opponents challenged the policy in federal court, arguing it violated the 14th Amendment, which was ratified in 1868 and guarantees citizenship to nearly anyone born on U.S. soil.

Immigration advocates celebrated the ruling outside the Supreme Court. Ana Marie Hernandez with the Florida Immigrant Coalition said the executive order created fear and confusion for many immigrant families. Among those following the case closely was 18-year-old Sindia, a recent high school graduate and full-time student whose parents immigrated from Guatemala in the early 2000s. Sindia said she panicked when Trump announced plans to end birthright citizenship, noting it was written in the Constitution that people born on U.S. soil are automatically granted citizenship. Supporters of Trump's proposal argued the 14th Amendment was never intended to apply to children born to parents without lasting ties to the United States. Unless Congress passes a constitutional amendment, birthright citizenship is expected to remain protected.

cards.headline: Boca Raton hosts 68th Independence Day celebration with full day of events
cards.teaser: Boca Raton's Fabulous Fourth 2026 returns with events throughout the day, including a Firecracker 5K, tennis and pickleball tournaments, and evening fireworks.
cards.body:
Boca Raton's 68-year-old Independence Day tradition returns on Saturday, July 4, 2026, with a full day of events celebrating America's 250th anniversary. The Fabulous Fourth 2026 schedule begins at 7:15 a.m. with a Firecracker 5K at Florida Atlantic University, 777 Glades Road, requiring $40 registration with no on-site registration available. At 8 a.m., the Liberty Cup Pickleball and Tennis Tournament starts, with pickleball at Patch Reef Park and tennis at The Racquet Center, featuring registration fees of $35 to $50 for pickleball and $35 to $43.75 for tennis.

From 1 to 4 p.m., the Fabulous Fourth Block Party takes place at Sugar Sand Park, 300 S. Military Trail, offering free admission with kids' crafts, yard games, a DJ and food trucks. The evening Fabulous Finale runs from 6:30 to 9:30 p.m. at Countess de Hoernle Park, 1000 Spanish River Blvd., featuring live music at 6:30 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. and a 20-minute fireworks display at 9:10 p.m. Free parking is available at Boca Raton Innovation Campus with entry from Yamato Road, and free trolley service runs from 6:30 p.m. through the end of the event. No pets, coolers, sparklers, drones, alcohol or glass bottles are permitted.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and pool party at North Palm Beach Country Club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
North Palm Beach is hosting a full day of Independence Day festivities on July 4 at the North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse. The free community event brings together family-friendly activities, entertainment and a fireworks display set to light up the sky at 9 p.m. According to organizers, this year's celebration carries special significance as the nation marks America's 250th anniversary, adding an extra layer of patriotic spirit to the traditional Palm Beach County holiday gathering.

The day's activities kick off at 11 a.m. with a community pool party at the country club pool area. Attendees can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, various games and activities, food and beverages, and a poolside satellite bar. Event organizers note that the pool deck and lawn areas will provide a festive atmosphere throughout the day. This extended pool party sets the tone for an afternoon filled with entertainment and recreation for visitors of all ages.

As the afternoon transitions into evening, additional activities take center stage starting at 4:30 p.m. Families can participate in lawn games such as cornhole, Connect 4 and giant Jenga, along with face painting and other interactive options. The Clubhouse will also open its doors at 4:30 p.m. to serve a Fourth of July barbecue buffet. Live music from the band Solstice Reign is scheduled to begin around 6 p.m., providing entertainment as guests enjoy their meals and continue participating in games and activities.

For those looking to catch the fireworks display, Ashley Shipman, the director of parks and recreation, recommends the golf course as one of the best vantage points to watch the 9 p.m. finale. The combination of the open landscape and elevated views makes it an ideal location to experience the pyrotechnic show. With activities spanning from mid-morning through the evening, the event offers something for everyone seeking to celebrate the holiday with family and friends in the North Palm Beach community.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting season programs through September
cards.teaser: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season this summer.
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The center's Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations during the programs may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. Loggerhead Marinelife Center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds surpasses $90 million in fundraising for Florida governor's race
hero.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds has surpassed $90 million in total fundraising, including $23 million raised in the last three months, further cementing his dominance in the GOP field.
hero.body:
Republican gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds has raised more than $90 million for his campaign, solidifying his position as the frontrunner in the GOP primary race. The Naples congressman announced the fundraising totals this week, which include $10 million in his official campaign account and $80 million raised through the Friends of Byron Donalds political committee. The money comes from approximately 37,000 donors. In the most recent three-month period alone, Donalds brought in $23 million. Ryan Smith, the campaign's chief strategist, emphasized Donalds' competitive advantages in the race. "While other candidates run on fumes, Byron Donalds is running full steam ahead," Smith said. "Byron is the clear conservative choice to lead Republicans into the General Election and crush the Democrats and their radical, unaffordable agenda."

The announcement of Donalds' fundraising success coincided with new endorsements from major Florida political figures. Incoming Florida Senate President Jim Boyd and Florida House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison both endorsed Donalds on the same day the fundraising numbers were released. Attorney General James Uthmeier, a former chief of staff to Governor Ron DeSantis, also announced his support for the candidate. Additionally, Donalds has secured an endorsement from President Donald Trump, who encouraged the congressman to enter the race. With Governor Ron DeSantis unable to seek reelection due to term limits, the governorship is open for the first time in eight years.

Donalds faces ten other GOP primary opponents seeking the Republican nomination, including Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, investment manager James Fishback, and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner. Despite criticism from rivals for declining to participate in planned primary debates, Donalds continues to maintain a substantial lead in polling. His campaign has begun an aggressive spending strategy, announcing a $20 million statewide advertising purchase across television and digital platforms. The campaign plans to launch two new television ads that will reach voters throughout Florida.

Beyond advertising, the Donalds campaign has emphasized grassroots organizing efforts. The campaign has already knocked on more than 180,000 doors across the state as it works to mobilize voters. The GOP primary election is scheduled for August 18 and will determine which Republican nominee advances to the general election in November.

cards.headline: 40-year corrections veteran Richard Comerford named Florida prison system chief
cards.teaser: Gov.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis has appointed Richard Comerford, a 59-year-old Crawfordville resident, as Secretary of the Florida Department of Corrections. Comerford succeeds Ricky Dixon, who retired Tuesday after 30 years with the department. Comerford began his FDC career in 1986 as a correctional officer at Okaloosa Correctional Institution and rose through the ranks holding multiple warden and assistant warden assignments across Florida. He most recently served as Deputy Secretary, providing executive oversight for the nation's third-largest state correctional system. As Assistant Deputy Secretary of Institutions, he directed operations for 96,000 incarcerated individuals, 19,000 staff, and 143 facilities. Comerford holds a bachelor's degree in criminology from the University of Florida and has completed executive training through the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, National Institute of Corrections, Florida Emergency Management Agency and American Correctional Association.

DeSantis praised Comerford's work history, calling him "instrumental in advancing the Department's mission." Comerford said he is "truly humbled" by the appointment. Dixon, appointed by DeSantis in November 2021 and later President of the American Correctional Association, praised his successor, saying the department is "in great hands" and noting Comerford's "fingerprints are on every major success our agency experienced." Comerford now leads a department with a more than $3.9 billion budget, nearly 23,400 full-time positions and about 151,000 inmates. He is an active member of the Florida Sheriffs Association and North American Association of Wardens and Superintendents, and has presented before the U.S. Department of Justice Review Panel on Prison Rape.

cards.headline: Florida Democrats move to intervene in Paula Stark ballot lawsuit
cards.teaser: The Florida House Democratic Campaign Committee and two Democratic candidates are fighting to join Republican Rep. Paula Stark's lawsuit to get back on the ballot after she failed to qualify last month.
cards.body:
The Florida House Democratic Campaign Committee and Democratic candidates Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves are seeking to join Republican Rep. Paula Stark's ballot access lawsuit. Mark Herron, the Florida Democrats' chief election lawyer, filed the motion to intervene on their behalf. According to the court filing, granting Stark's requested relief would substantially affect the candidacies of the two Democratic candidates who qualified for House District 47 and would impact the resources the FHDCC expends for that election. Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried stated Wednesday that hundreds of candidates statewide filed their paperwork on time, while Stark is spending thousands of taxpayer dollars on a lawsuit due to her own mistake.

Stark filed a response this week opposing the Democrats' motion to intervene in her lawsuit against Secretary of State Cord Byrd, Osceola Supervisor of Elections Mary Jane Arrington and Orange County Supervisor of Elections Karen Castor Dentel. Stark argued the two Democrats have no direct interest in her qualifying paperwork and that their concern about resource allocation does not establish the direct and immediate interest required for intervention. Stark is suing in Leon Circuit Court after failing to qualify for the ballot last month. She claims one required form was hand-delivered in Tallahassee but was inadvertently returned to her campaign treasurer and significant other Joel Davis. The traditionally blue district covers St. Cloud, east Kissimmee and a small portion of Orange County.

cards.headline: U.S. Rep. Jimmy Patronis opposes House online safety bill as too soft on Big Tech
cards.teaser: Florida Congressman Jimmy Patronis voted against the Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act this week, calling it a Big Tech bill endorsed by Big Tech that fails to hold companies accountable.
cards.body:
The bipartisan Kids Internet and Digital Safety (KIDS) Act passed the House this week on a 267-117 vote after contentious debate, but U.S. Rep. Jimmy Patronis opposed the measure as insufficiently tough on tech companies. Patronis voted no and has continued pushing an alternative bill he introduced in January, the Promoting Responsible Online Technology and Ensuring Consumer Trust (PROTECT) Act, which would fully repeal Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act. That provision shields companies from lawsuits related to criminal activity using their social media platforms. "This is the Big Tech bill endorsed by Big Tech," Patronis said, adding that the companies target children, profit from their attention, and escape accountability because of Section 230 protections.

The KIDS Act package includes several initiatives from Florida lawmakers. These include the Kids Online Safety Act championed by Republican U.S. Rep. Gus Bilirakis, the Safe Internet for Minors Act introduced by U.S. Rep. Laurel Lee of Thonotosassa, and the Children and Teens Online Privacy Protection Act that Lee co-led. U.S. Rep. Kathy Castor, a Tampa Democrat who previously led resistance to the bill from her position on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, ultimately supported the final legislative package. "This is an important step, but it is not the end of our work," Castor said. The bill now moves to the U.S. Senate before going to President Donald Trump for his signature.

cards.headline: Florida Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson wins nursery industry endorsement
cards.teaser: FNGLA-PAC, the political arm of the Florida Nursery, Growers and Landscape Association, endorsed Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson's re-election bid.
cards.body:
FNGLA-PAC, the political arm of the Florida Nursery, Growers and Landscape Association, is endorsing Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson's re-election bid. The endorsement puts the nation's largest nursery, greenhouse and landscape association firmly in Simpson's corner. The group represents more than 1,700 member businesses and thousands of industry professionals tied to a sector that generates a $41.9 billion economic impact and supports more than 279,000 jobs across the state.

Throughout his tenure, Simpson has been a steadfast advocate for Florida's nursery and landscape industry, according to Tal Coley, FNGLA's chief executive officer. Coley pointed to Simpson's responsiveness, noting the Commissioner has consistently listened to members and worked alongside the industry to elevate key issues, whether advocating for disaster recovery assistance following hurricanes and severe weather events or supporting policies that protect the industry's ability to choose the right equipment. Simpson welcomed the endorsement, saying Florida's nursery and landscape industry is vital to the agricultural economy and communities. FNGLA-PAC describes itself as a bipartisan fund dedicated to boosting visibility and lending campaign support to state legislators and candidates who back the green industry.

cards.headline: Florida State Parks Foundation expands accessible amenities across park system
cards.teaser: The Florida State Parks Foundation announced this month a new wave of accessible boardwalks, observation platforms and all-terrain chairs coming soon to parks across the state.
cards.body:
Paula Russo, a longtime member of the Florida State Parks Foundation who has advocated for outdoor accessibility for more than 30 years, contracted polio as a baby in 1953 and uses a wheelchair. She said there was a time when people who use assistive devices or who have limited mobility could not get out on the beach, swim in a spring, or board a river or ocean tour boat. The Florida State Parks Foundation, working with the Florida Park Service and community partners, has made significant progress in expanding accessible amenities across the state park system.

Accessible river boats are now in service at Silver Springs and Wakulla Springs with ample room for several mobility devices. Beach wheelchairs are available at every coastal state park, and some parks offer floating wheelchairs that provide access to the ocean. All-terrain wheelchairs that can traverse mud, rocks, roots and sand open more than 1,600 total miles of trails and greenways across the state. William J. "Billy Joe" Rish Recreation Area in Northwest Florida is specifically designated to provide recreational opportunities for people with disabilities. July is Disability Pride Month, a time to celebrate and commemorate the signing of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

cards.headline: Ben Butler secures Okeechobee firefighters endorsement in Congressional District 9 race
cards.teaser: The Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of Okeechobee endorsed Ben Butler in his bid to unseat a Democratic incumbent in Florida's 9th Congressional District.
cards.body:
The Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of Okeechobee, IAFF Local 2918, is endorsing Ben Butler in his bid for Florida's 9th Congressional District. A representative of the local said first responders need leaders who respect the sacrifices made by firefighters, law enforcement officers, and EMTs every day, and that Butler has demonstrated that commitment throughout his career. Butler said firefighters run toward danger while others run away, and they do not ask who is calling or what political party they belong to. The endorsement adds a first-responder stamp to Butler's hometown-heavy list of supporters.

Butler raised more than $200,000 in his first eight days in the race and has rolled out endorsements from Okeechobee County's Sheriff, Mayor, County Commission and School Board. A ninth-generation Floridian who helped build Butler Oaks Farm into a multigenerational dairy and cattle operation, Butler was first named to the South Florida Water Management District Governing Board by Gov. Ron DeSantis in 2019 and reappointed in 2024. He holds bachelor's and master's degrees in Animal Science from the University of Florida and has built his campaign around a producer-not-politician pitch.

hero.headline: Boys & Girls Clubs of Martin County Introduce 200 Kids to Tennis Through NJTL Program
hero.body:
The NJTL Boys & Girls Clubs of Martin County introduced more than 200 children to tennis through the First Serve experience. The program brought youth from the community together to learn the sport.

The National Junior Tennis and Learning network operates the program through the Boys & Girls Clubs of Martin County. USTA Florida announced the First Serve initiative brought tennis instruction to local children.

The First Serve experience provided youth in Martin County with an introduction to tennis fundamentals. The program gave children who may not otherwise have access to tennis instruction an opportunity to try the sport.

The NJTL program works with Boys & Girls Clubs locations to provide tennis programming to young people across the community. The initiative continues the organization's mission to use tennis as a tool to reach youth in underserved areas.

cards.headline: Woman Killed in Hobe Sound Mobile Home Fire Identified
cards.teaser: Authorities have identified a woman who died in a mobile home fire in Hobe Sound.
cards.body:
A woman was killed in a mobile home fire in Hobe Sound, according to authorities. Officials have now identified the victim of the fire.

The fatal fire occurred at a mobile home in the Hobe Sound area of Martin County. Investigators worked to determine the victim's identity following the blaze.

Authorities released the name of the woman who died in the fire. The investigation into the mobile home fire continues.

cards.headline: Two Killed After Tesla Hit From Behind on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County
cards.teaser: Two people died following a rear-end collision involving a Tesla on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County.
cards.body:
Two people were killed after a Tesla was struck from behind on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County. The fatal crash occurred on the turnpike running through the county.

The Tesla was hit from behind by another vehicle on the turnpike. Both occupants of the Tesla died as a result of the collision.

Authorities responded to the crash scene on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County. The collision resulted in two fatalities.

cards.headline: University of Florida Board of Governors Confirms Stuart Bell as 14th President
cards.teaser: The University of Florida Board of Governors has confirmed Dr. Stuart Bell as the university's 14th president.
cards.body:
The University of Florida Board of Governors confirmed Dr. Stuart Bell as the 14th president of the university. Bell previously served at the University of Alabama for a decade.

The board approval concludes a two-year search for a new president at the University of Florida. Bell will take over leadership of the state's flagship university in Gainesville.

Bell's confirmation marks the end of the presidential search process that began two years ago. He will assume the presidency after his tenure at the University of Alabama.

hero.headline: Property listed at 5051 N Highway A1a in Fort Pierce

A property located at 5051 N Highway A1a Apt 9-5 in Fort Pierce, FL 34949 appeared in a real estate listing on Realtor.com early Wednesday morning. The listing provides information about the property's availability.

Norman E Godfrey of Fort Pierce died recently, according to an obituary posted Tuesday. Yates Funeral Home and Cremation Services in Fort Pierce is handling arrangements.

cards.headline: Kolter Homes adds layout options in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: Kolter Homes announced expanded home design personalization with new layout options in Port St. Lucie.

Kolter Homes announced Tuesday it is expanding home design personalization with new layout options in Port St. Lucie. The builder is offering additional floor plan configurations for buyers.

The announcement was made through Newswire.com on Tuesday. Further details about specific layout options and communities were not provided in the release.

The event also features a 4's on the 4th Volleyball Tournament from 8 a.m. to noon on the south end of the municipal beach, a sand sculpting contest sponsored by Delray Beach Rotary and Kiwanis Clubs, and snorkeling and scuba dive tours of the S.S. Inchulva Delray Wreck from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. Boca Raton's 68-year-old Independence Day tradition returns with a full day of events. cards.headline: St. Lucie County receives high marks in Florida school grades
cards.teaser: Florida released school grades Wednesday showing St. Lucie County, along with Indian River and Martin counties, scored high marks.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County received high marks in the latest Florida school grades released Wednesday, according to Treasure Coast News. Indian River and Martin counties also scored high in the state evaluations.

The grades were released by the Florida Department of Education on Wednesday. Specific grade levels and school performance data for St. Lucie County schools were not detailed in the initial report.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after drug search
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce man was arrested after deputies found drugs during a search, according to WPBF.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce man was arrested Wednesday after St. Lucie County deputies found drugs during a search, WPBF reported. The arrest occurred following a law enforcement operation in Fort Pierce.

Deputies conducted the search that led to the drug discovery and arrest. Specific charges and the suspect's identity were not provided in the initial report.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce drug bust yields 60.5 grams meth, 43.5 grams MDMA
cards.teaser: Law enforcement found 60.5 grams of methamphetamine and 43.5 grams of MDMA in a trafficking bust in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
Law enforcement discovered a trafficking stash containing 60.5 grams of methamphetamine and 43.5 grams of MDMA in Fort Pierce, WPEC reported Wednesday afternoon. The quantities found meet Florida trafficking weight thresholds for both substances.

The bust occurred in Fort Pierce during a law enforcement operation. Arrest details and suspect information were not provided in the initial report.

hero.headline: Indian River County Schools Offer Free Meals at 6 Campuses
hero.teaser: Indian River County schools will offer free meals at six campuses.
hero.body:
Indian River County schools will provide free meals at six campuses. The program addresses nutritional needs for students during the summer.

The district has designated six specific school sites to offer the meals. Parents and students can access the free food at these campus locations.

The summer meal program helps ensure students have access to nutrition when regular school meal services are not available. The program operates at multiple school facilities across Indian River County.

cards.headline: Delray Beach Opens 50-Year-Old Time Capsule During Fourth of July Celebration
cards.teaser: Delray Beach will open a historic time capsule during its Fourth of July celebration on Saturday, the same capsule that was sealed and buried in 1976 when Ameri.
cards.body:
A piece of local history buried for half a century will be unearthed this weekend in Delray Beach. The city will open a historic time capsule during its Fourth of July celebration on Saturday, the same capsule that was sealed and buried in 1976 when America celebrated its 200th birthday. The capsule contains memories, messages and artifacts from a past generation.

David E. Randolph, a former city council member who was in office when the capsule was sealed, contributed one item to the time capsule: a collection of his thoughts about his race, his education, and his highlights and awards. The time capsule ceremony begins at 5 p.m. Saturday at Atlantic Avenue and A1A as part of Delray Beach's Fourth of July festivities. The annual celebration draws more than 20,000 people and features food trucks, vendors, children's activities, live music, and a fireworks show at 9 p.m. After the ceremony, items from the time capsule will go on display, with the city planning to showcase select pieces at the Delray Beach Historical Society.

cards.headline: Federal Audit Flags Spending at Indian River Lagoon National Estuary Program
cards.teaser: A federal audit has identified spending concerns at the Indian River Lagoon National Estuary program.
cards.body:
Federal auditors have flagged spending at the Indian River Lagoon National Estuary program. The audit examined financial practices and expenditures at the environmental organization.

The Indian River Lagoon National Estuary program oversees conservation and restoration efforts for the lagoon system. The waterway spans multiple counties including Indian River County.

The audit findings raise questions about how federal funds designated for lagoon protection have been managed. The program plays a key role in environmental management efforts for the lagoon ecosystem.

cards.headline: Florida School Grades Released: Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin Score High
cards.teaser: State education officials released school grades, with Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin counties posting strong results.
cards.body:
Florida has released school grades for the academic year, with Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin counties scoring high marks. The grades measure academic performance across all three Treasure Coast counties.

The results show strong educational outcomes in the region. School districts use the state grades to assess performance and identify areas for improvement.

The grades evaluate student achievement and school progress based on standardized testing and other metrics. All three Treasure Coast counties performed well in the statewide assessment.

cards.headline: Marcus & Millichap Brokers $5.3 Million Sale of Multifamily Property in Vero Beach
cards.teaser: A Vero Beach multifamily property has sold for $5.3 million in a transaction brokered by Marcus & Millichap.
cards.body:
Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of a multifamily property in Vero Beach for $5.3 million. The commercial real estate firm handled the transaction for the residential complex.

The sale represents investment activity in the Vero Beach housing market. The property provides multiple residential units in the Indian River County city.

Multifamily property transactions reflect ongoing investor interest in Treasure Coast rental housing. The $5.3 million price tag indicates the value of residential rental properties in the Vero Beach area.

cards.headline: Road Closures Begin Thursday for 4th on Flagler Celebration in West Palm Beach
cards.teaser: Drivers in downtown West Palm Beach should prepare for road closures beginning Thursday afternoon ahead of the annual 4th on Flagler celebration.
cards.body:
Drivers in downtown West Palm Beach should prepare for road closures beginning Thursday afternoon ahead of the annual 4th on Flagler celebration. Starting at 4 p.m. Thursday, July 2, several roads in the downtown area will close and remain closed through Sunday, July 5, according to the City of West Palm Beach.

The following roads will be closed: South Flagler Drive from Banyan Boulevard to Lakeview Avenue, the 100 blocks of Clematis Street, Datura Street and Evernia Street, the 200 blocks of Fern Street and Tanglewood Court, the 100 and 200 blocks of Trinity Place, Chase Avenue from Lakeview Avenue to South Flagler Drive, and Narcissus Avenue from Fern Street to Evernia Street. Drivers are encouraged to plan ahead, allow extra travel time and use alternate routes while the closures are in place. The annual 4th on Flagler celebration features live entertainment, family activities, food vendors and a fireworks display along the downtown waterfront. Residents can find additional information about traffic impacts and event details on the city's website.

cards.headline: Vacant Nordstrom at Mall at Wellington Green Could Become 620-Unit Apartment Complex
cards.teaser: A plan has been submitted to transform the vacant Nordstrom at the Mall at Wellington Green into a large apartment complex, the village confirmed.
cards.body:
Bainbridge Companies has submitted plans to convert 18 acres of the vacant Nordstrom store at the Mall at Wellington Green into a 620-unit multifamily apartment complex. If approved, the existing building would be demolished to make way for the development, which Village Manager Jim Barnes said would include one-, two- and three-bedroom units, shared amenities, three towers and a parking structure. Barnes stated the project addresses a housing shortage extending beyond the county throughout the state and beyond.

Some Wellington residents oppose the proposal. Richard Meyers, who has lived in Wellington for more than a decade, said the area already has numerous apartment complexes around the mall and expressed opposition to adding more. Other residents raised concerns about traffic impacts, with Gaby Martinez suggesting the added density could create bottlenecks on local roads. Barnes noted that several anchor stores at the mall continue to perform well, stating that Macy's, Dillard's and JCPenney are high-performing stores, and that the Macy's location is the highest-performing store in the state. No timeline or cost estimate for the project has been announced, and the plans have not been approved.
